history.period: Associated event 1688; site memorialised later; SGPC control from 1956
history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Gurudwara Nada Sahib stands on the banks of the Ghaggar river in Panchkula, in the Shivalik foothills. Guru Gobind Singh halted here in 1688 while travelling from Paonta Sahib to Anandpur Sahib after the Battle of Bhangani; a Lubana villager, Nadu Shah, served the Guru and his followers with food and milk, and the Guru blessed the place to be known by his name. The spot remained obscure until Bhai Motha Singh raised a platform there; the shrine was under the Patiala and East Punjab States Union Dharmarth Board in 1948 and taken over by the SGPC in 1956. The complex now has a two-storey domed structure, a large meeting hall, langar hall (free community kitchen), pilgrim rooms, and a 105-ft Nishan Sahib staff; Amrit Sanchar is performed on Puranmasi. CSV TOWN AND STATE BOTH WRONG: actual town Panchkula, state Haryana (not Chandigarh/Punjab).

name: Gurudwara Nada Sahib
town_description: Panchkula is a planned city and district headquarters in Haryana, forming the eastern part of the Chandigarh Tricity alongside Chandigarh and Mohali. It sits on the Ghaggar river at the foothills of the Shivaliks, known for its sectors, the Morni Hills nearby, and religious sites along the riverbank. The gurdwara lies in Panchkula, about 10-15 km from central Chandigarh.
